**Tesla – recent whirlwind of developments (late Oct 2026)**  

- **Fatal crash involving Full Self‑Driving (FSD)** – On Oct 22 a Tesla on I‑80 in Vallejo (California) hit and killed a 71‑year‑old pedestrian; dash‑cam footage shows the car attempting to brake and steer before the impact [1][7].  
- **Rebranding of FSD in Europe** – Tesla renamed its Full Self‑Driving system “Tesla Assisted Driving” for the European market, a move reported on Oct 9 [19].  
- **Roadster “flying” debut** – Mid‑Oct Tesla unveiled a new Roadster that allegedly uses SpaceX‑style thrusters, claiming 0‑60 mph in under a second; the claim generated viral videos and mixed commentary [15‑17].  
- **Roadster reservation uncertainty** – On Oct 18 Tesla warned that it “cannot guarantee” reservation holders will ever receive a Roadster, fueling concern among buyers [13].  
- **Q3 earnings slump** – Tesla’s third‑quarter profit fell 43%, and the stock dipped >2% despite selling more EVs than produced and erasing a surplus of unsold inventory [9][8].  
- **Cybercab rollout plan** – Tesla announced it will begin selling its autonomous “Cybercabs” to transport firms by year‑end, expanding the robotaxi business [10].  
- **Musk’s broader strategy** – Elon Musk reiterated his vision of world‑wide autonomous travel dominated by Tesla cars and hinted at a possible merger with SpaceX, a theme appearing across multiple Oct 22 reports [2][4][5][6][11][12].  

*Overall picture*: Tesla is juggling a high‑profile safety incident, a rebrand of its driver‑assist tech, ambitious product launches (Roadster, Cybercabs), a sharp earnings decline, and ongoing speculation about a merger with SpaceX—all within the span of the past two weeks.
